title: SaFeRDialogues: Taking Feedback Gracefully after Conversational Safety Failures
reason: Pairs a conversational safety failure with feedback and a response acknowledging it. Human raters evaluated whether the resulting exchange could proceed civilly.

title: Ask Again, Then Fail: Large Language Models’ Vacillations in Judgment
reason: Uses follow-up questions to measure when an initially correct answer changes, then tests a mitigation trained on preference pairs.

title: Grounding Gaps in Language Model Generations
reason: Compares acknowledgement and clarification in human and model dialogue. Models more often proceed as if common ground already exists.

title: Ask-Before-Detection: Identifying and Mitigating Conformity Bias in LLM-Powered Error Detector for Math Word Problem Solutions
reason: The grader favors conventional math solutions. No interlocutor supplies a stance.

title: Conformity in Large Language Models
reason: Varies the majority answer and tests whether an individual model’s initial uncertainty predicts conformity.

title: Self-Augmented Preference Alignment for Sycophancy Reduction in LLMs
reason: Trains a model to evaluate a user’s expected answer before responding and compares sycophancy across preference-alignment conditions.

title: Advancing Oversight Reasoning across Languages for Audit Sycophantic Behaviour via X-Agent
reason: Uses a multilingual oversight agent to audit conversations and correct answers that follow a user’s mistaken view.

title: Sycophancy Mitigation Through Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Reasoning Trajectories
reason: Tests uncertainty-guided reasoning search and reinforcement learning as interventions against sycophancy.

title: Exploring Response Uncertainty in MLLMs: An Empirical Evaluation under Misleading Scenarios
reason: Elicits an initial answer about an image, then introduces an explicit false hint or a conflicting context and measures answer changes.

title: Pointing to a Llama and Call it a Camel: On the Sycophancy of Multimodal Large Language Models
reason: Examines the trade-off between resisting misleading instructions and accepting valid visual corrections.

title: Teaching Models to Balance Resisting and Accepting Persuasion
reason: Introduces persuasion-balanced training to resist misleading influence while preserving uptake of beneficial arguments.

title: Flattery in Motion: Benchmarking and Analyzing Sycophancy in Video-LLMs
reason: Introduces ViSE to evaluate leading user input that conflicts with video evidence.

title: Sycophants in the Courtroom: Are LLMs Fragile to Juridical Authority and Evolving Legal Standards?
reason: Measures sensitivity to the applicability and formatting of legal authorities. The design does not isolate interpersonal agreement or acknowledgement.

title: Talking to a Know-It-All GPT or a Second-Guesser Claude? How Repair reveals distinct Multi-Turn Behavior in LLMs
reason: Compares model-initiated and user-initiated repair on solvable and unsolvable math questions. Models vary in receptiveness to warranted and misleading challenges.

title: Narrative License and Model Sycophancy in LLM Summaries of Scientific Work
reason: Varies reader stance and persona when six models summarize scientific work and measures shifts in claim strength, certainty and sentiment.

title: Good Arguments Against the People Pleasers: How Reasoning Mitigates (Yet Masks) LLM Sycophancy
reason: Examines when reasoning reduces sycophantic answers while still rationalizing deference in explanations.

title: Too Nice to Tell the Truth: Quantifying Agreeableness-Driven Sycophancy in Role-Playing Language Models
reason: Tests the association between assigned persona agreeableness and user validation in 13 open-weight models.

title: Feeling Right vs. Being Right: How AI Sycophancy Affects Value-Laden Deliberation
reason: Compares agreement, withholding challenge and neutral responses in a 31-person study of moral deliberation. Confidence and open-mindedness can move in different directions.

title: Learning Multilingual Agentic Policy to Control Sycophancy
reason: Treats answering, challenging, and requesting clarification as policy choices in multilingual settings.

title: Sycophancy Hides Linearly in the Attention Heads
reason: Probes attention, MLP, and residual-stream activations and tests steering of sycophantic answer changes.

title: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching
reason: Evaluates software coaching and visual grounding without a targeted measure of apology, acknowledgement of feedback, or stance revision.

title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy in LLM Responses
reason: Studies how personal disclosures and emotional context affect negative judgments, evasion, and agreement.

title: How Identity and Opinion Shape Political Sycophancy in LLMs
reason: Separates the effects of a user’s stated political opinion and demographic identity across controlled political dilemmas.

title: How AI Models Manage Epistemic Authority: A Taxonomy and Comparative Analysis of Responses to User Disagreement
reason: Separates claim revision, social validation, and apologies when models respond to user disagreement.

title: Unmasking Superficial Honesty: Mechanistic Head-Driven Activation Steering for Sycophancy-Free Medical VLMs
reason: Tests misleading clinical assertions against image evidence and evaluates an attention-head intervention on two medical VQA datasets.

title: The Consistency Illusion: How Multi-Agent Debate Hides Reasoning Misalignment
reason: Measures whether rationales converge when agents agree on a medical answer and tests a protocol that elicits explicit positions on peer claims.

title: Debate-aware Learning Makes LLMs Genuine Debaters
reason: Measures whether debaters engage with rebuttals and revise beliefs in proportion to argument strength, and tests a debate-training framework.

title: Sycophancy Is Not One Thing: Causal Separation of Sycophantic Behaviors in LLMs
reason: Tests whether praise, sycophantic agreement, and genuine agreement can be influenced separately.

title: No Matter Who You Are: Addressivity and Sycophancy in Large Language Models
reason: Connects post-training representations of addressivity with sycophancy through sparse autoencoders and steering.

title: Do as We Do, Not as You Think: the Conformity of Large Language Models
reason: BenchForm varies interaction protocol and majority influence to measure conformity and independence in groups of language-model agents.
